title.narrative: Youth 2030 Cities: Localization of the SDGs By and For the Youth

description.narrative:
The Youth 2030 Cities project began in October of 2021 in collaboration with the Healthy Cities for Adolescents (Botnar) Program, a Fondation Botnar initiative. The objective of the project is to promote the localization of the SDGs through strengthening of local youth capacity to partner with local governments to co-create evidence-based interventions and engage in overall city governance. The project aims to enable meaningful participation of young people in governance and urban planning activities, the localization of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and New Urban Agenda (NUA).
As Youth 2030 Cities expands to become a programme, it will continue to grow its activities and provide young people and their communities and organizations with training and opportunities to engage in governance and participate in an evidence building process. The focus is done through scaling up of key project outputs such as expanding the Promising Practices on an annual basis, the review and scaling up of the National DeclarACTIONs and aggregate Global DeclarACTION, and the development and deployment of the SDGs Scorecard application to support youth and youth-led orgnisations’ involvement in the monitoring and reporting of the SDGs, and to encourage youth and local government partnerships to facilitate city-wide SDG progress towards Agenda 2030 on an ongoing basis. In 2022-2024, normative tools will be refined and further developed from tools piloted in the first Phase of the programme - tools such as SDG Cities Training for youth in partnership with the Capacity Development Unit, and the SDGs Scorecard, an impact measurement and reporting App for young people and local governments to collaborate and co-create solutions towards the achievement of the SDGs,
as well as new tools addressing issues of capacity building for youth organisations and financing / fundraising for SDG localization programmes.
Youth 2030 Cities was done in parallel to and jointly with UN-Habitat’s SDG Cities Flagship programme, with joint missions being undertaken, programmes developed, partners engaged, and tools such as the SDGs Scorecard and the City Scan tool designed,tested and developed. This internal partnership continues, as well as new partnerships such as the Game Changer Initiative, which will see a joint research programme developed and implemented, which focuses on youth and the localization of the SDGs.
These activities have resulted in meaningful youth engagement in local and global dialogues, such as the High-Level Meeting on the Acceleration of the New Urban Agenda (April 27-29, 2022), and the World Urban Forum (June 26-30, 2022). For the new Youth 2030 Cities initiative, a focus will be on creating policy impact in key global events such as the ECOSOC Youth Forum and the UN-Habitat Assembly. At the National and city level, events such as the upcoming urban forums in Ecuador, Senegal and Ghana will be targeted. The aim is to both continue a deeper dive into the policy realm with current alumni cities, and expand the initiative to 4 more countries as determined by UN-Habitat and Fondation Botnar.
